expected_observations.expected_pattern: One limit path gives an attractive relation while another leaves an explicit unknown or failure.
expected_observations.observable: whether the qualitative gap or decay statement survives the target limit order
expected_observations.what_it_would_teach: The next experiment should test uniformity, not generate another fixed-regulator derivation.
expected_observations.what_would_disconfirm_it: A cutoff- and volume-uniform estimate that commutes with the spectral readout.

failure_modes: The thought experiment remains too abstract and never names F(a,L,t).
The follow-up treats a limit-order warning as a proof of failure.
Uniformity requirements are not attached to a topology or observable sense.

followup_cycle_tasks.description: Try to construct a simple F(a,L,t) where fixed-regulator decay fails to commute with continuum transfer.
followup_cycle_tasks.failure_or_demotion_criterion: If no such class is possible under the branch assumptions, promote the uniformity premise as plausible but still unproved.
followup_cycle_tasks.situation_title: A limit-order switchboard for cutoff, volume, and long-time behavior
followup_cycle_tasks.success_criterion: A counterexample class explains why the active branch needs uniform control.

insight_hypotheses: The branch should rank uniformity experiments above additional fixed-regulator calculations.
Noncommuting limits are stop/backtrack criteria only after the uniformity rescue attempt fails.

interventions.decision_value: If the conclusion changes under limit order, the branch must backtrack to a uniformity lemma.
interventions.operation: Exchange the long-time limit with cutoff and volume limits.
interventions.predicted_direction: A fixed-regulator spectral gap may disappear or fail to transfer if estimates are not uniform.

criteria_met: The branch moves from fixed regulator statements to continuum or infinite-volume commitments.
Changing limit order can decide whether the qualitative claim is target-relevant or a regulated artifact.
criteria_missing: The topology or observable sense of convergence still has to be named.
need_assessment.why_not_direct_derivation_or_probe: A direct fixed-regulator derivation would not reveal whether the conclusion commutes with the target limit order.

proposed_graph_updates.rationale: Thought experiment challenges transfer unless cutoff, volume, and long-time limits commute in the stated topology.

situation.controlled_contrast: Compare lim_{t to infinity} lim_{a to 0,L to infinity} F with lim_{a to 0,L to infinity} lim_{t to infinity} F.
situation.mathematical_carrier: A family F(a,L,t) with fixed-regulator decay, finite-volume spectral discreteness, and a continuum-transfer question.
situation.minimal_world: Imagine three knobs a, L, and t where each pairwise route looks controlled, but the conclusion changes when t tends to infinity before a tends to zero or L tends to infinity.
non_claims: This does not assert which order is correct for the target.
This does not replace a uniform estimate.
This only identifies what uniformity a later proof attempt must supply.
situation.purpose: Make noncommuting limits visible as a branch-control issue.
situation.title: A limit-order switchboard for cutoff, volume, and long-time behavior
situation.why_this_situation_is_informative: It exposes whether a claimed qualitative relation is a real target property or only a path-dependent regulated artifact.

transfer_scope.does_not_transfer: Any final conclusion about the target limit.
transfer_scope.transfer_certificate_needed: A named topology or observable sense in which the limits are taken.
transfer_scope.transfers: A branch-control diagnostic: whether the next cycle should ask for a uniformity lemma.

trigger_criteria: The branch moves from fixed regulator statements to continuum or infinite-volume commitments.
Changing limit order can decide whether the qualitative claim is target-relevant or a regulated artifact.

variants.changed_condition: Assume a bound independent of a and L over the required t range.
variants.predicted_change: The limit-order obstruction should weaken or disappear.
variants.reason_for_variant: Identifies the exact kind of estimate that would rescue the branch.
